name: Robust and fair predictions
gist: Papers on making models work reliably across different groups and conditions, handling noisy data, and making predictions that don't discriminate.
explain: A model that works perfectly on clean, typical data might fail catastrophically when things are different. A self-driving car trained on clear roads fails in rain. A face recognition system trained on faces of one skin tone fails on others. A loan-approval system trained on historical data might perpetuate past discrimination. You need models that work reliably even when conditions change, that treat different groups fairly, and that do not hide their failures under the assumption that the world will always be as clean as the training data.

The hard part is that reliability and fairness require balancing many competing demands. A model that works reliably across different conditions often becomes less accurate on typical data. A model that is perfectly fair in one sense (equal accuracy for all groups) might be unfair in another sense (equal outcomes across groups, even if it means treating people differently). And you cannot always measure fairness directly — you might not even have labels for the groups you care about, or the groups might be defined in complex ways. You also have to decide whether to aim for reliability when conditions change naturally or when someone is actively trying to fool the model.

Researchers work on reliability by training on diverse data that includes edge cases, by using techniques that make the model's predictions stable (small changes in input should lead to small changes in output), and by designing models that can detect when they are out of their depth. They work on fairness by auditing models for bias, by explicitly optimizing for fairness metrics, by debiasing training data, and by building in transparency so people understand what the model is doing and can contest its decisions. Some focus on worst-case reliability (making sure the model never fails dramatically) while others focus on average reliability (making sure it works well across different conditions on average).

papers.title: Beyond Match Maximization and Fairness: Retention-Optimized Two-Sided Matching
papers.contribution: Maximizes user retention as the ultimate objective, providing an alternative to match maximization or fairness-based approaches.

papers.title: FERD: Fairness-Enhanced Data-Free Adversarial Robustness Distillation
papers.contribution: Achieves improved fairness and robust stability in adversarial robustness distillation across public datasets through principled proportion and distribution adjustments.

papers.title: Fairness-Aware Multi-view Evidential Learning with Adaptive Prior
papers.contribution: Achieves more balanced evidence allocation and improves both prediction performance and reliability of uncertainty estimation on six real-world multi-view datasets.

papers.title: Robust Spiking Neural Networks Against Adversarial Attacks
papers.contribution: The method significantly enhances SNN robustness in adversarial scenarios while reducing gradient sparsity and state-flipping vulnerability.

papers.title: Causal-aware Anomaly Detection for Tabular Data
papers.contribution: CausalAno shows consistent improvements across 28 tabular datasets (18 continuous-only and 10 mixed-type), comparing against 16 strong baselines.

papers.title: Noise-Aware Generalization: Robustness to In-Domain Noise and Out-of-Domain Generalization
papers.contribution: Significantly improves performance by leveraging cross-domain information to better distinguish label noise from natural domain shifts.

papers.title: Robust Federated Inference
papers.contribution: The composition of adversarial training and test-time robust aggregation surpasses existing robust aggregation methods by 4.7-22.2% in accuracy across diverse benchmarks.
